lesson-intro.text: Monkeys love them, and so do lunchboxes. A banana is two long curves that meet at the ends, like a moon lying on its back. Watch it bend, then peel off one of your own.

top-edge.text: The top of the banana is a long, gentle curve. Dip down in the middle and rise up to the right.

bottom-edge.text: The belly curves deeper. From the left end, swing down low and up to meet the top line.

cap.text: The stem is a little square cap on the left end. Up, across and back down.

tip.text: The other end has a tiny dark tip. Draw a short hook to close it.

ridges.text: Bananas have edges along their skin. Draw two long lines inside that follow the belly.

brown.text: The stem and the tip are brown.

lesson-outro.text: One yellow banana with a brown stem. Just don't slip on the peel.
